Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

attractive adjective

appealing: an offer, an idea, a price

also appealing, tempting, inviting, an attractive offer, an attractive idea, desirable, seductive, alluring

classical

Cic. Phil. 7.7
Cic. de Or. 1.221: expetenda atque optābilia (Lewis & Short)

optābilis, optābile

Declension on Wiktionary

desirable, to be wished for

What one would wish to have; optābile est ut, it would be ideal if.

Other words

  • illecebra, illecebrae f. — an attraction, an enticement

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 43: maxima est illecebra peccandi impūnitātis spēs (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A lure, in a good or a bad sense; a favourite word of Cicero’s. What makes an offer attractive is its illecebra.

  • illecebrōsus, illecebrōsa, illecebrōsum — full of allurement, very enticing

    also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 1.1.54 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 149: alluring; Traupman 157 · Declension on Wiktionary

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.; then late (Prud., Amm.))

Examples

  • cuique pāx, praesertim cīvīlis, quamquam omnibus bonīs, tamen in prīmīs fuit optābilis

    to whom peace, civil peace above all, though desirable to all good men, was more desirable than to anyoneCic. Phil. 7.7

See also attractive, condition.

SourcesLewis & Short: optabilis · Lewis & Short: illecebra · Lewis & Short: illecebrosus
